clue.text: It's as likely as not to see mogs back-to-back (one Manx?)

indicators.note: a Manx cat famously has no tail, so the last letter of the word for a male cat is docked

parts.note: one of the mogs, a male cat, is a tom

indicators.note: the cats are placed back to back, so the word for a cat is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat, as is puss

explanation.surface: A cat fancier's odds of spotting two moggies sitting back to back, perhaps including a tailless one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' docks the tail of TOM to leave TO; 'back-to-back' turns PUSS into SSUP. Mog is British slang for a cat; a Manx cat is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is an even chance, a matter as likely to go one way as the other, like a coin flip.

clue.text: Balloon that may be edible?

definitions.meaning: to balloon is to swell or grow rapidly, the verb sense
a fungus, some kinds of which can be eaten

explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to expand fast, and a mushroom is a fungus that is often eaten.

clue.text: Dirty clothing ending on floor, so awkward

indicators.note: clothing a thing means wrapping round it, so the soiled word goes round a letter

parts.note: dirty means stained

indicators.note: ending on a word points to its final letter

explanation.surface: Grubby clothes left lying on the floor make for an uncomfortable scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts R, the last letter of floor ('ending on'), inside STAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained manner or atmosphere is forced and uneasy, which is to say awkward.

clue.text: Piano piece that's more soppy

definitions.meaning: a felt pad in a piano that stops a string vibrating

explanation.definitionFit: A piano has dampers to silence its strings, and something wetter is damper.

clue.text: Call girl often about opening of restaurant behind hospital

indicators.note: behind places the following group after the hospital letter
about means the phrase for often surrounds a letter

parts.note: often means a lot

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman of the night frequently hangs about a restaurant entrance near the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R (first of restaurant, from 'opening of') inside A LOT; 'behind' puts that after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A harlot is an old-fashioned word for a prostitute, of whom a call girl is one kind.

clue.text: Investing 10p in entire broadcast, not good enough

indicators.note: investing means clothing or wrapping around, so the scrambled word is put round the coins
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of entire are rearranged

parts.note: 10 is X in Roman numerals and p is the abbreviation for penny or pence

explanation.surface: Putting tenpence into a whole radio broadcast is a poor, amateurish effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' reads like a financial word next to 10p; here it means wrapping round, with the scramble of entire (from 'broadcast') going round the coin letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexpert lacks skill, so their work falls short of a good enough standard.

clue.text: Source of water beginning to trickle in laundry, wrung completely

parts.note: a well is a place water is drawn from

indicators.note: in places the first letter of trickle inside the anagram
wrung means twisted, so the letters of laundry are rearranged
beginning to a word means its first letter

explanation.surface: Laundry wrung out thoroughly, with water starting to drip from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of water' tempts as a spring; WELL is it. 'wrung' scrambles the laundry, and 'in' sets the trickle's first letter (from 'beginning to') among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Well and truly is an idiom meaning thoroughly or utterly, so it means completely.

clue.text: God admitting false alibis about right for appeal

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the god word takes in the rest

parts.note: a god is a deity

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters surround the letter for right
false signals the letters of alibis are made up into something else

explanation.surface: A god lets in some phoney alibis concerning the right to appeal a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'about' wraps the scrambled alibis (from 'false') round the right letter, and 'admitting' sets that whole group inside the god word.
explanation.definitionFit: Desirability is the quality of being attractive or wanted, which is what appeal means.

clue.text: Declines badly, being cut off

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of declines are arranged poorly into something new

explanation.surface: Someone's health worsens badly and they are cut off in their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Being silenced is being stopped from speaking, just as a speaker is cut off mid-sentence.

clue.text: Sounds like something painful afoot for author John

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for a painful foot ailment is spoken, giving the name

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the big toe joint

explanation.surface: A sore foot is put forward as the name of a writer called John.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan was the seventeenth-century English writer of The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: Stuff including wettest odd bits discarded?

definitions.text: Stuff including wettest odd bits discarded?

indicators.note: including means the word for stuff takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to stuff is to jam or cram

indicators.note: throwing out the odd-numbered letters of a word keeps only the even ones

explanation.surface: Waterlogged odds and ends thrown away, washed up on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits discarded' keeps the even letters of wettest, and 'including' puts them inside the jam word; read whole, the clue also describes flotsam's partner on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard, the soaked discarded stuff that washes ashore.

clue.text: North American native, partner of the fish friar, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say means the phrase is spoken, sounding like the animal

parts.note: fish's partner is chip, as in fish and chips, and a friar is a monk

explanation.surface: Asks what native creature could be the sidekick of a monk who fries fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Friar Tuck and a fish fryer; read the pun as chip plus monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The chipmunk is a small striped squirrel native to North America.

clue.text: Girl on current lifting apparatus

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a current of air is wind
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman rides on an air current, swept up by a lifting device.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch, a drum turned to haul up ropes and loads.

clue.text: Vessel — or a chamber on it?

definitions.meaning: a long low ship rowed by oars

explanation.definitionFit: A galley is both an oared ship and the cooking room on board any vessel.

clue.text: Cost better in egg production?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to beat another hen at laying

explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is an expense, and to out-lay is to surpass in laying eggs.

clue.text: Elegant plunge, down onto sleazy establishment

indicators.note: in a down clue, onto means the first word sits on top of the second

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a dive is a seedy bar or club

explanation.surface: Knocking back a drink before heading into a seedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A swallow dive is a graceful dive with arms outspread, so it is an elegant plunge.

clue.text: Rising in Spanish food, brown smoke

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the Spanish dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A tanned diner gets up from Spanish food to light a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the brown word upwards, and 'in' puts it inside the Spanish rice dish; a smoke is a cigar here, not a puff.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, something one smokes; smoke is slang for a cigar or cigarette.

clue.text: Cake something wearied American's gobbled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read in the upward direction
gobbled means swallowed, so the letters are held inside the words

explanation.surface: A tired American wolfs down some cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gobbled' finds ARIEDAM inside wearied American's, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira cake is a plain, firm sponge, named for its traditional pairing with Madeira wine.

clue.text: Inch left inside plane, perhaps

indicators.note: inside places the letter for left within the other word

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface, like a side of a solid figure

explanation.surface: Inching inside an aircraft, perhaps to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' wants to be an aircraft; it is a flat face, a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along stealthily, and to inch is to move slowly in small steps.

clue.text: Strike male

explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to strike forcefully, and a ram is a male sheep.

clue.text: Draw a line under some cricket reject

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the second word sits below the first

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
to rule is to draw a straight line

explanation.surface: An instruction to underline part of a cricket report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw a line under' looks like an idiom for ending something; it splits into RULE plus a position indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule is to reject or set aside a decision by superior authority.

clue.text: Democrats' donkey, for example, as a socialite?

definitions.meaning: the donkey is the US Democratic Party's emblem, so it is literally an animal of a political party
someone who loves going out to parties

explanation.definitionFit: A party animal is a keen partygoer, and the Democrats' donkey is literally a political party's animal.

clue.text: Talent of an infant playing football?

definitions.meaning: babies are good at letting saliva run from the mouth
running with the ball at one's feet

explanation.definitionFit: Dribbling is both drooling, as babies do, and moving a football along with small kicks.

clue.text: Disease, one caught by North African on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above
caught by means the numeral is held inside the North African word

parts.note: a Berber is one of the indigenous peoples of North Africa
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A North African on an island catches a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' holds the numeral inside the North African people's name, and 'on' sets that group above the island letter, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by a lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine).

clue.text: Files, items spotted among lidless rubbish receptacles

indicators.note: among means the spotted items go in the middle
lidless means the top letter is taken off, as a lid is the top of a bin

parts.note: bins hold rubbish
dice are cubes marked with spots

explanation.surface: Spotted items found among rubbish bins with their lids missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lidless' removes the top letter of the bins, and 'among' puts the spotted cubes inside what is left; 'Files' is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Indices are indexes, ordered lists or catalogues of records, much like files.

clue.text: Familiar form of snack is near nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of is near are jumbled

explanation.surface: A homely snack is close to some nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the snack; it is the signal to rearrange IS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich, an informal word for a snack.

clue.text: Butterfly's breathtaking marking?

definitions.meaning: a European butterfly with ragged wings and a white ...-shaped mark
a punctuation mark where a reader may pause to take breath

explanation.definitionFit: The comma is both a butterfly species and the punctuation mark showing a pause.

clue.text: Heads of sheep always down low

indicators.note: heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Sheep always grazing with heads lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like part of the definition; it is the last word picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means feeling down or sad, a synonym.
